Author: Hill
Title: Crossroads of highly pathogenic H5N1: overlap between wild and domestic birds in the Black Sea-Mediterranean impacts global transmission
study_design: Satellite telemetry tracking of wild ducks, influenza A virus screening and sequencing, phylogenetic/phylogeographic analyses, and spatiotemporal analysis of overlap between duck utilization distributions and reported HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks.
wildlife_species: Common Teal (Anas crecca); Northern Shoveler (Anas clypeata); Common Shelduck (Tadorna tadorna); Northern Pintail (Anas acuta); Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos); Eurasian Wigeon (Anas penelope); Common Pochard (Aythya ferina)
diseases_or_pathogens: Highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1; Low pathogenic avian influenza H1N1; Low pathogenic avian influenza H7N7; Low pathogenic avian influenza H10N9
interface_statement_verbatim: The interface between wild ducks and HPAI H5N1-infected poultry increased in late winter and peaked during early spring when birds move between habitats to form larger flocks and fed intensively to gain condition for migration.
interface_statement_section: 4.3 Overlap between poultry and waterfowl peaks during spring migration
